data.title: Define explicit expectations after amending mappings
data.when: When adding or modifying data mapping rules between two systems or structures where the resulting state is not immediately obvious from the code changes alone.
procedure: Identify the source and target objects/schemas involved in the mapping amendment.
Determine the specific, non-obvious expected output state (e.g., a required field must be null; a calculation must round up; a relationship status must transition).
Implement a dedicated validation step or assertion immediately following the mapping application that explicitly verifies this calculated/expected state against the actual resulting data structure.
Ensure this new expectation check is included in the automated test suite run.
pitfalls: The system appears to pass tests locally but fails in CI/CD because an implicit business rule or constraint (the 'expectation') was violated by the mapping change.
Assuming that simply running unit tests covering input-output pairs is sufficient, thereby missing state transitions or data validation errors.
verification: The entire task (adding and deploying the amended mapping) runs end-to-end successfully on the lower-tier automation flow.
A new explicit assertion related to the expected post-mapping state is required, confirming that the system cannot complete the task without this step.
